cards.explanation: The answer is the worshipers there. John, who is seeing these visions, is told, “Go and measure the temple of God and the altar, and count the number of worshipers there.” (Revelation 11:1) So it's a measuring job AND a headcount. I'd want a clipboard for that one.

The answer is False. John is told to leave out the courtyard outside the temple, and the text says, “Do not measure it, because it has been given over to the nations…” (Revelation 11:2) So the reason is that the courtyard has been given over to the nations. It never says anything about being too holy to measure. When the Bible hands you the reason, you take the reason it hands you.
The answer is trample. The nations “…will trample the holy city for 42 months.” (Revelation 11:2) It's a time with a number on it. Trampling is walking heavily right over something.
The answer is sackcloth. The two witnesses will prophesy for 1,260 days, “…clothed in sackcloth.” (Revelation 11:3) Sackcloth is rough, plain cloth. That's a long stretch of days to wear it.

The answer is that it devours their enemies. If anyone wants to harm the two witnesses, “…fire proceeds from their mouths and devours their enemies.” (Revelation 11:5) The text says it plainly. These two are protected.

The answer is True. The two witnesses have “…power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy…” (Revelation 11:6) The days of their prophecy is that same stretch of time, the 1,260 days. That's a lot of sky to be in charge of.

The answer is blood. The two witnesses have power “…to turn the waters into blood…” (Revelation 11:6) That's one big power, and it comes right alongside shutting the sky. Just reading it makes me want to check the faucet.

The answer is the beast. “…the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them…” (Revelation 11:7) The text says it plainly. This happens once the two witnesses have finished their testimony. The beast is the one who comes up from the Abyss in this verse.

The answer is True. The beast “…will wage war with them, and will overpower and kill them.” (Revelation 11:7) I think this is a heavy part, and I'll say it plainly. But this verse isn't the end of the story, friends, so hold on.

The answer is crucified. The bodies of the two witnesses will lie in the street of the great city, “…where their Lord was also crucified.” (Revelation 11:8) The text gives that detail right alongside the city's figurative names, Sodom and Egypt. It's a sober line, so we'll keep it simple.

The answer is the bodies to be laid in a tomb. For three and a half days, all peoples and tribes and tongues and nations “…will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.” (Revelation 11:9) That's the one thing the text says they refuse. I think it's a hard thing to picture, so we'll just move along gently.

The answer is True. Those who dwell on the earth “…will gloat over them and celebrate and send one another gifts…” (Revelation 11:10) The verse gives the reason too. It says these two prophets had tormented them.
The answer is tormented. Those who dwell on the earth celebrate “…because these two prophets had tormented them.” (Revelation 11:10) The text gives the reason in the same breath. Plain and direct.

The answer is the breath of life from God! “…the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses, and they stood on their feet…” (Revelation 11:11) After three and a half days, the whole scene turns around. I love this verse. It reads like a plot twist that God wrote.

The answer is False. The text says, “…they stood on their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them.” (Revelation 11:11) No cheering is mentioned. After all that celebrating, I think the mood changes fast.

The answer is up to heaven in a cloud. The two witnesses hear a loud voice from heaven say, “Come up here.” And “…they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them.” (Revelation 11:12) Their enemies are watching as it happens. I'd love to see their faces.

The answer is tenth. In the great earthquake, “…a tenth of the city collapsed.” (Revelation 11:13) It happens in the same hour the two witnesses go up. The text gives the fraction, and we keep it exactly.

The answer is that they are terrified and give glory to God. After the earthquake, “…the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.” (Revelation 11:13) I think that's a big shift after all the gloating earlier. The text puts the terror and the glory together in one breath.

The answer is that the world's kingdom has become the Lord's! When the seventh trumpet sounds, the voices in heaven say, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ…” (Revelation 11:15) That's the big news of the whole passage.
The answer is True. The voices in heaven go on, “…and He will reign forever and ever.” (Revelation 11:15) Forever and ever. That's the last word of the announcement.

The answer is that they fall on their faces and worship God. The twenty-four elders “…who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God…” (Revelation 11:16) They respond by worshiping. That's a good example for all of us to follow.

The answer is that He has begun to reign. The elders say, “…because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.” (Revelation 11:17) That's their reason for giving thanks. They say it right to Him.
The answer is judge. The elders say, “The time has come to judge the dead…” (Revelation 11:18) It's right there in their words. Heavy words, so I'll say it simply and move on.

The answer is False. The elders say the time has come “…to reward Your servants the prophets, as well as the saints and those who fear Your name, both small and great…” (Revelation 11:18) The prophets are named, and so are the saints and those who fear His name. The word only doesn't fit, so there's room at the table for more.

The answer is to destroy those who destroy the earth. The elders finish by saying it's time “…to destroy those who destroy the earth.” (Revelation 11:18) That's the last thing on their list. I'm sticking with their exact words.

The answer is ark. When God's temple in heaven was opened, “…the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple.” (Revelation 11:19) The text puts the ark's appearing right there. I'll just let that line sit there.

The answer is lightning and thunder and hail. When the temple in heaven opens, “…there were flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.” (Revelation 11:19) Lightning, thunder and hail are all in that list. Quite a finish for the whole passage, friends.
